slot.brief: Draw the structure of a substituted cycloalkene or alkene (figure) and ask for the carbonyl fragment(s) obtained after ozonolysis with reductive workup.

stem: The alkene shown undergoes ozonolysis followed by reductive workup with $\text{Zn}/\text{H}_2\text{O}$. The products are:

verdicts.working: Reductive ozonolysis cleaves the C=C: the carbon bearing two methyl groups gives propanone, and the carbon bearing H and an ethyl group gives propanal.

working:
$\text{CH}_3\text{C(CH}_3)=\text{CHCH}_2\text{CH}_3 \xrightarrow[\text{Zn}/\text{H}_2\text{O}]{\text{O}_3} \text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3 + \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}$
Alkene carbon with two carbon substituents $\to$ ketone; alkene carbon bearing H $\to$ aldehyde.

Independent check: Reductive ozonolysis cleaves the C=C: the carbon bearing two methyl groups gives propanone, and the carbon bearing H and an ethyl group gives propanal.
solution:
Reductive ozonolysis cleaves the C=C bond; a carbon bearing two carbon groups forms a ketone, while one bearing H forms an aldehyde.
$$\text{CH}_3\text{C(CH}_3)=\text{CHCH}_2\text{CH}_3 \xrightarrow{\text{O}_3,\,\text{Zn}/\text{H}_2\text{O}} \text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3 + \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}$$
The products are propanone and propanal.
